prompts.name: memory
prompts.synthetic_prompt: Explain to a systems programmer how CPU cache locality, memory bandwidth, instruction dependencies, and NUMA placement interact when multiplying matrices. Use a concrete toy example with two CPU sockets and a batch of independent vectors. Distinguish measurements from assumptions. Discuss why adding cores sometimes helps and sometimes does not. Write several connected paragraphs with enough detail to guide a small experiment, using only general computer-science reasoning.

prompts.name: python
prompts.synthetic_prompt: Write a small Python implementation of a bounded least-recently-used cache with get and put operations, then explain its invariants. Use a dictionary and an ordered list so the example is readable without imports. Describe the empty-cache case, updating an existing key, eviction when capacity is reached, and capacity zero. Include a short example sequence and explain which key is evicted at each step. This is fictional educational code, not a production deployment.

prompts.name: japanese-network
prompts.synthetic_prompt: 架空の家庭内ネットワークを説明してください。PCが2台とサーバーが1台あり、全て有線スイッチにつながっています。初心者向けに、IPアドレス、サブネット、デフォルトゲートウェイ、名前解決の役割を順番に説明し、同じネットワーク内の通信とインターネットへの通信を具体例で比較してください。設定変更を指示するのではなく、通信がどの順番で進むかを文章で説明してください。説明は数段落で、用語は初出時に短く定義してください。

prompts.name: math
prompts.synthetic_prompt: Give an elementary proof that the sum of the first n odd positive integers equals n squared. Start with a geometric picture described in words, then give an algebraic induction proof. Explain the base case and the induction step separately. Include checks for n equal to 1, 2, and 5, and finish by explaining why examples alone do not prove the claim for every positive integer. Keep the derivation self-contained and use clear mathematical notation.

prompts.name: sql
prompts.synthetic_prompt: Create a fictional SQL example with customers and orders. Show a small schema, a query for the total completed-order amount per customer, and an explanation of why a left join can preserve customers with no completed orders. Explain the difference between putting the order-status condition in the join and in the where clause. Include null handling and a stable ordering of the result. Do not connect to any real database; all names and records should be invented.

prompts.name: schedule
prompts.synthetic_prompt: Design a simple algorithm for scheduling independent jobs on two identical workers. Each job has a known duration, jobs cannot be split, and workers start together. Explain a greedy longest-job-first method, walk through durations 9, 8, 7, 6, and 4, and discuss why the heuristic is not a proof of global optimality. Include pseudocode, an invariant about assigned work, and how you would test the algorithm on edge cases. Keep the example purely hypothetical.

prompts.name: japanese-story
prompts.synthetic_prompt: 短い創作を書いてください。舞台は雨の日の小さな図書館です。古い地図を整理している司書と、町の橋について調べに来た学生の会話を中心にしてください。実在の人物や地名は使わず、会話の途中で二人が地図の書き込みに気づく展開にしてください。派手な事件ではなく、観察と対話で小さな謎が解ける話にします。最初に情景を一段落書き、その後に会話と短い動作描写を交互に続けてください。

prompts.name: testing
prompts.synthetic_prompt: Describe a test plan for a fictional text editor undo-and-redo feature. Define the expected behavior when edits are made, several undo actions occur, and a new edit is made before redo. Include examples for insertion, deletion, replacing a selection, empty history, and consecutive edits grouped into one action. Explain which properties can be checked automatically and which user-interface details require separate inspection. Use clear prose and small examples without depending on any particular editor implementation.
